implementation: Raw .data() access detaches writable nested array storage once, marks exposed locals in the checker to prevent borrowed record/parameter views, and makes copied private closure environments independent when mutation occurs through element pointers. Explicit shared captures still share their binding. Narrowed aliases and mutable loop places resolve to their owning storage.

limits: Native 64-bit host. Warm filesystem caches; one build per binary.
C graph uses flat edges and a handwritten map; Dewy uses per-node arrays and an insertion-ordered map.
String equality uses separately allocated payloads; C uses pointer/length pairs and libc memcmp, Dewy uses runtime strings.
Kernel times exclude input generation; wall times include the complete process.
Thread CPU timing excludes descheduling, but CPU frequency and cache contention still matter.

measurement_notes: All initial and focused matched samples are retained; rechecks cover the unresolved large-default and Dunes compilation comparisons.
All eight runtime workloads retain their accepted artifacts in both modes, with fresh boundary and full-size checks. Their timing and C ratios are unmeasured at this stage.

The fix intentionally changes programs that use writable raw data through fields, indices, aliases or captures; unchanged benchmark artifacts are performance evidence for those workloads, not a byte-compatibility requirement.
Implementation-language read-only parameters/iteration and temporary-value raw views retain their existing policy. Ownership tests edit ordinary iteration values through explicit local copies.
The fresh root-source throughput target of 250k lines/s and broad C/Rust runtime goal remain unmet.
